The Sky Keeper grew lonely watching over this dim realm. She had no companion except her own reflection in the still waters below. One day, she wept, and her tears fell like silver rain. But instead of reaching the earth, each tear froze in the cold upper air, suspended between heaven and ground.

Now, whenever someone feels isolated in the dark, they need only look up to see the Sky Keeper's gift: proof that even loneliness, when shared, can illuminate the world.

Long ago, when the world was newly formed, a young goddess named Lyra possessed the most beautiful voice in all creation. She would sing to the mountains, the rivers, and the sky, filling the earth with melodies that made flowers bloom and stars shimmer brighter.

But Lyra was lonely. She sang alone, with no one to answer her songs.

One day, she climbed the highest mountain and sang her most sorrowful melody, pouring her heart into every note. She sang of her isolation, her longing for companionship, her wish for someone—anyone—to sing back to her.

The mountain, moved by her pain, decided to help. It caught her voice in its ancient stone chambers and sent it back to her, repeating her final notes.

Lyra gasped in wonder. For the first time, she heard her own voice returned to her. Overjoyed, she sang again, and again the mountain answered.

From that day forward, mountains and canyons everywhere learned to return voices to those who called out. The goddess Lyra had found her companion, and though it was only her own voice reflected back, she never felt alone again.

This is why lonely places always answer when we call—they remember Lyra's gift.

One winter, a young wanderer became lost in Kael's caverns, singing to keep warm and brave. Her voice drifted down through the tunnels, and Kael heard music for the first time. Enchanted, he began to hum along, his deep voice harmonizing with hers.
